evidence: src/infrastructure/ProductController.ts getStock: reads req.params.productId, calls getProductStockUseCase.execute(productId) and returns res.json(response). This is transport/adapter work that belongs in infrastructure.
src/infrastructure/ProductController.ts getAllStock: calls getProductStockUseCase.executeAll() and wraps the result as { products: response }. This only shapes the HTTP response.
Both handlers catch errors and map them to res.status(404|400).json({ error }). This is translating errors into HTTP responses, which belongs in transport code, and no business rules are involved.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: ProductController is an Express HTTP adapter sitting in the infrastructure layer. It does transport work only: it pulls productId out of the request params (and handles the case where it arrives as an array), hands off to GetProductStockUseCase, sends the result back as JSON, and turns exceptions into HTTP error responses with status 404 or 400. None of that is business logic. It doesn't calculate stock, check domain invariants or touch persistence. Picking the status code from the error is ordinary adapter-level error translation. Every responsibility in the file fits an infrastructure/transport adapter.
